claims.text: Tungsten-based materials are intended for use as fusion plasma-facing components.
In baseline tungsten-based plasma-facing materials at high temperature, plastic strain is governed predominantly by stress-assisted dislocation climb controlled by lattice diffusion.
In baseline tungsten-based plasma-facing materials at high temperature, toughness is governed predominantly by lattice-diffusion-controlled dislocation climb.
Systematically changing the lattice diffusion rate will directly modulate the rate of plastic deformation.
Systematically changing the lattice diffusion rate will directly modulate toughness.
Isotopic substitution can change the lattice diffusion rate or diffusion activation energy while leaving other relevant microstructural factors constant.
Thermal pre-treatment can selectively change the diffusion activation energy while leaving other relevant microstructural factors constant.
Fusion plasma-facing materials are required to operate at temperatures of at least 1000 K.
Jogged dislocation configurations are indicative of dislocation climb.
At high temperature, enhanced lattice diffusion makes stress-assisted dislocation climb feasible.
The rate of stress-assisted dislocation climb sets the plastic strain rate.
Increasing lattice diffusion will accelerate dislocation climb and increase plastic strain rate.
Increasing lattice diffusion will reduce apparent toughness.
Faster dislocation climb reduces toughness by diminishing the material's ability to blunt crack tips.
Dynamic recrystallization can confound interpretation of the creep or deformation mechanism.
The proposed mechanism applies broadly to refractory-metal alloys above 1000 K when recrystallization and phase transformations do not dominate.
Tungsten has very low fracture toughness and exhibits brittle transgranular and intergranular failure regimes.
Yield strength and ductility can serve as proxies for toughness in the proposed comparison.
A controlled comparison should use samples with identical baseline microstructures and identical temperatures and stresses, differing only in lattice diffusion rate.
The hypothesis is falsified if changing the diffusion rate produces no systematic or statistically significant change in plastic strain rate or toughness under otherwise identical conditions.

contradictions.description: The mechanism associates faster climb with greater plastic flow and strain accommodation, but then predicts reduced toughness through diminished crack-tip blunting. The hypothesis does not explain how increased plastic accommodation would diminish rather than enhance crack-tip blunting.
